AIOS Software Engineering Handbook

Architecture, requirements, interfaces, safety, data, resource planning, and the engineering evidence in one file.

The current plan distinguishes the whole-product estimate (133–195 person-days) from provisional remaining work (95–160 person-days). GP2 exact date and team availability remain unconfirmed.

28 architecture and software diagrams · 52 requirement records · Source-linked technical content

01 Project and software boundary

AIOS is an autonomous Ubuntu user-space resource-management design. It observes host and process state, requests generic predictions, applies policy and safety checks, and admits only bounded resource actions.

What AIOS does

The software runs alongside Linux. A process can receive a LEAVE decision, a recommendation, or a proposal for bounded CPU-weight control. Although decisions are process-aware, the initial operating-system control targets an approved workload cgroup. The design does not equate a process with a cgroup.

Human access

People inspect status, recommendations, safety health, and audit projections through a read-only dashboard. Runtime commands, action approvals, policy edits, mode changes, and direct actuator access are outside that user-facing boundary.

Baseline

Ubuntu 24.04 is the proposed target. OBSERVE_ONLY is the default. The final product target monitors CPU, RAM, and I/O and may apply bounded cpu.weight, memory.high, and supported io.weight/io.max changes on approved cgroups, each behind its own capability and safety gate. Implementation is phased, with CPU first; memory and supported I/O follow host and workload review. Unsupported controls remain recommendations. Inference internals remain generic because their model-level design belongs to the AI workstream.

Reading this handbook

This file combines the software design, complete requirements records, diagrams, engineering rationale, interface notes, evidence interpretation, resource analysis, and management plan. Proposed contracts and numerical gates retain their design status. The measured example is a passive Ubuntu 26.04.1 VM capture; it does not establish target-version compatibility or AIOS performance.

Diagrams are embedded. Select a diagram to open its full-size view. Editable diagram definitions and collector code are included in expandable sections. Use Ctrl+F to search the document. The source register at the end identifies the local artifacts incorporated into this edition.

02 Requirements and traceability

The software requirements use hierarchical identifiers such as 1.1.2. The specification states the scope and constraints; the record set preserves priorities, verification methods, legacy IDs, and evidence basis.

Software requirements specification

AIOS Software Requirements Specification

Hierarchical requirements baseline for an Ubuntu 24.04 research prototype

Version 2.0 | Status: proposed draft for team review | Updated 14 November 2026

Purpose and status

This SRS defines a proposed autonomous user-space system for observing resource pressure and, only when a reviewed host-local profile permits it, applying bounded CPU-weight changes on approved Ubuntu cgroups. OBSERVE_ONLY is the default. People can view status and audit projections through a read-only dashboard; they cannot command, approve, reconfigure, or directly control AIOS. This document describes requirements and verification ideas, not completed implementation, validated market demand, or measured benefit.

Requirements use hierarchical identifiers such as 1.1.2. Each leaf is intended to state one verifiable outcome. The hierarchical identifiers are the sole requirement IDs used across the current project baseline.

1. System purpose and boundary

AIOS collects host/process CPU, RAM, I/O, and pressure telemetry; validates freshness, units, quality, and process identity; stores bounded local telemetry in SQLite; passes a generic evidence window to inference services; forms a per-process LEAVE or recommendation; and applies a policy gate. Only an admitted bounded request may cross the authenticated local socket. The actuator revalidates the peer, target, ownership, bounds, and matching resource capability before using a fixed adapter; it verifies read-back and records outcomes. The final product target covers independently gated CPU, RAM, and supported I/O controls. Implementation is phased, with CPU first. A watchdog blocks new writes and requests guarded recovery.

The intended deployment is one Ubuntu 24.04 host using systemd and cgroups v2, subject to prerequisite checks. Optional eBPF collection and optional AIOS CPU affinity/quota profiles require separate host review. The inference boundary remains generic; model types, algorithms, model-specific fields, and internals are not specified here.

BoundaryIncludedExcluded or unresolved
Human accessRead-only status, recommendations, mode/safety health, action outcomes, and audit projections.Commands, action approval, policy edits, mode switches, and direct resource control.
Initial OS controlBounded cpu.weight changes for preconfigured approved cgroups.memory.max writes, process termination, I/O control writes, arbitrary shell, or unapproved targets.
Interfacespsutil/Linux observations, optional fixed eBPF probes, SQLite, generic inference boundary, Unix socket/SO_PEERCRED, cgroups v2, FastAPI query projections, systemd.Exact API routes, socket payload schema, database schema, service accounts, and numeric safety thresholds.

2. Candidate market and operating context

The package now covers five candidate operating contexts: interactive Linux workstations, shared development/build/test hosts, constrained or edge Linux nodes, single-node/containerized cgroup-managed services, and university lab/demo hosts. These are scope hypotheses for research planning, not validated customer segments or claims of adoption.

The market matrix contains 18 need hypotheses, each linked to one or more candidate contexts, an existing technical approach or alternative, source IDs, a proposed AIOS response, hierarchical requirement IDs, an evidence limitation, and a local validation question. Official documentation and prior systems research show that resource pressure and control mechanisms exist; they do not show that a target user wants AIOS or that AIOS improves outcomes. No local interviews, survey responses, TAM/SAM/SOM, market size, willingness-to-pay, adoption, or performance claims are supplied.

Candidate contextWhy it is in scope to investigateEvidence status
MS-01 Interactive Ubuntu/Linux desktops and workstationsCandidate context where CPU or memory pressure may affect foreground responsiveness.Technical fit: PSI/cgroups documentation [S1,S2]. No evidence that this segment wants AIOS.
MS-02 Shared development, build, test, or research Linux hostsCandidate context where concurrent jobs may compete for CPU and make diagnosis or prioritization difficult.Mechanism evidence: cgroups/systemd [S2,S3]. Prior scheduling research [S7,S8]. Demand remains unvalidated.
MS-03 Constrained or edge Ubuntu/Linux nodesCandidate context where AIOS resource overhead could be material and host configuration may be limited.Technical trade-off evidence from CPU control and affinity docs [S3,S6]. No host-specific fit or benefit measured.
MS-04 Single-node or containerized Linux services governed by cgroupsCandidate context where resource groups are visible but may already be managed by a runtime or orchestrator.Technical evidence: cgroup/systemd/Kubernetes resource behavior [S2,S3,S11]. AIOS orchestration integration is out of scope unless separately agreed.
MS-05 University labs and shared demonstration hostsCandidate context for reproducible demonstrations and resource attribution across controlled workloads.Project/rubric context only; no external evidence of adoption or local need.

Existing approaches to compare

The project should compare against the mechanisms already available on a target host rather than present them as absent competitors. PSI exposes pressure information; cgroup v2 and systemd expose configurable controls; systemd-oomd can take configured reactive memory-pressure action; Kubernetes manages container requests/limits when it is present. AIOS is a proposed layer and must not change a workload manager's target without explicit ownership and review.

AlternativeDocumented capabilityComparison boundary
Linux PSIExposes CPU, memory, and I/O pressure-stall information for supported scopes.A pressure signal is not itself a future forecast or a policy decision.
cgroup v2 and systemd resource controlsProvide CPU weights, quotas, and CPU-set controls subject to hierarchy and host configuration.Mechanisms do not by themselves provide AIOS predictions, per-process explanation, or project-specific safety review.
systemd-oomdUses cgroup v2 and PSI for configured reactive memory-pressure actions and may terminate an eligible cgroup.Its configured memory-pressure response is not the same as AIOS prediction or CPU-weight control.
Kubernetes resource requests and limitsThe scheduler and runtime use declared requests/limits; Linux runtimes typically enforce via cgroups.Orchestrator-level desired state may conflict with an independent host controller.
Manual monitoring and static host policyPotential existing approach for diagnosis and fixed resource limits/weights.Actual tools, effort, and perceived gaps vary by host and have not been collected.
AIOS proposed designGeneric inference outputs feed a per-process decision and bounded policy; only an admitted CPU-weight proposal can reach the guarded actuator.No implementation, prediction result, safety outcome, user demand, or performance benefit is established here.

4. Requirements conventions

ID format is section.subsection.leaf. Section 1 contains functional/system behavior; section 2 contains quality constraints and evidence requirements. Must means required for the proposed initial scope, Should means preferred design quality, and Could means optional/later. Priority does not mean implementation status. Each row in Ammar_Requirements_Traceability.csv carries a verification method, evidence limitation, provisional stakeholders, and status.

Acceptance ideas do not invent exact message formats, database columns, API paths, service names, numerical bounds, sampling intervals, or roles. Where a numeric gate is needed, this SRS requires it to be measured and approved before active control, but does not fabricate a value.

5. Functional requirements

Each numbered leaf is a proposed requirement. Verify it using the method recorded in the traceability CSV; status remains pending until evidence is collected.

1.1 Telemetry acquisition

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.1.1The collector shall record host and eligible-process CPU observations using supported read-only Linux interfaces and preserve the source and unit for each value.MustInspect a captured run; verify source, unit, timestamp, and host/process scope for every emitted CPU field.
1.1.2The collector shall record available host and eligible-process memory observations and mark each metric with its source, unit, and scope.MustCompare emitted fields with the selected Linux interface; verify unavailable values are statused rather than represented as zero.
1.1.3The collector shall record available host and eligible-process I/O observations with device or cgroup scope and interval context where the source requires deltas.MustInspect consecutive samples and confirm scope, units, interval, and counter-reset behavior are preserved.
1.1.4When supported by the running kernel and target, the collector shall read CPU, memory, and I/O Pressure Stall Information and identify unsupported or inaccessible resources.MustOn a host with supported PSI, demonstrate readings; on unavailable or denied sources, verify an explicit quality state.
1.1.5Optional eBPF collection shall remain disabled unless a fixed probe set has been reviewed, configured, and approved for the target kernel.ShouldInspect the default service configuration and verify no probe attaches unless the approved profile is selected.
1.1.6Each sample shall carry a UTC timestamp and a monotonic ordering value sufficient to detect ordering across wall-clock adjustment.MustSimulate or inspect wall-clock adjustment while confirming monotonic sample order is preserved.

1.2 Identity and data quality

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.2.1A process-scoped observation shall include PID and process start-time identity so a reused PID is not treated as the same process instance.MustExercise process exit and PID reuse or a controlled fixture; confirm prior identity and action context are not reused.
1.2.2Before inference or policy evaluation, the pipeline shall validate required field shape, unit, source health, and counter-delta validity.MustSubmit malformed, unit-mismatched, reset, and source-error samples; each is rejected or marked unusable with a reason.
1.2.3The pipeline and read-only view shall distinguish measured zero from unavailable, permission-denied, stale, warming-up, and degraded data states.MustFor each quality state, verify stored/viewed output does not collapse it into measured zero.
1.2.4A reset counter, missing interval, stale sample, or changed process identity shall invalidate dependent deltas and prevent those values from authorizing an action.MustInject reset, missing interval, stale age, and identity change; verify LEAVE/deny and no OS write.

1.3 Persistence and read projections

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.3.1Accepted telemetry shall be stored locally in SQLite for bounded inspection and recent-window access.MustInspect a run database and confirm accepted samples can be queried by run/time without an external service.
1.3.2Telemetry retention, database size, and SQLite write-ahead-log growth shall be bounded by reviewed host-local settings.MustRun a retention/size scenario; verify cleanup and cap behavior and report the selected settings.
1.3.3Dashboard data access shall use a read-only projection and shall not receive the actuator socket or cgroup write permission.MustInspect service permissions and attempt write/control operations through the dashboard boundary; both must be unavailable.

1.4 Inference boundary and decisions

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.4.1The telemetry-to-inference boundary shall pass approved observations and receive generic prediction outputs without prescribing model type, algorithm, or internals.MustReview the shared interface with AI owners; confirm no model-specific field or algorithm assumption is imposed by this SRS.
1.4.2A prediction used for a decision shall remain associated with its source window and available time/quality context; exact fields and schema require team agreement.MustTrace one output to its input window and freshness context without requiring a physical schema in this SRS.
1.4.3Inference outputs shall not write to the operating system or call the privileged actuator directly.MustInspect process permissions and exercise an inference output; only the decision/policy path may submit a bounded request.

1.5 Policy admission and action scope

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.5.1For each eligible process and evaluated window, the decision service shall produce LEAVE or a proposal/denial outcome with a reason.MustInspect outcomes for safe no-op, insufficient evidence, and eligible proposals; each must have a reason and target context.
1.5.2Before admitting a proposal, policy shall check operating mode, target eligibility, allowlist membership, evidence freshness, action bounds, and cooldown.MustExercise each gate independently and in combination; any failed gate yields denial and no write.
1.5.3OBSERVE_ONLY shall be the default at first start and after restart, missing/invalid configuration, or failed safety health; no dashboard action shall enable control.MustRestart with absent, malformed, and valid reviewed host-local configuration; only the reviewed valid configuration may permit the proposed bounded profile.
1.5.4The product target shall monitor CPU, RAM, and I/O and support bounded cpu.weight, memory.high, and supported io.weight/io.max actions on approved cgroups. Each control shall require its own capability and safety gate. Implementation is phased, with CPU first; unsupported controls remain recommendations.MustInspect all actuator paths and deny any unapproved cgroup, control file, or out-of-range value.
1.5.5AIOS shall apply only approved, bounded, resource-specific controls after their matching capability and safety gates pass. Unsupported controls remain recommendations. AIOS shall not write memory.max, terminate processes, or invoke arbitrary commands.MustInspect permissions and negative tests; verify each out-of-scope action is denied and audited.

1.6 Authenticated actuation

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.6.1Decision/policy-to-actuator requests shall use a host-local Unix domain socket.MustInspect runtime configuration and confirm the action path does not expose a network control endpoint.
1.6.2The actuator shall authenticate the connecting local process with SO_PEERCRED and reject peers outside the reviewed local peer policy.MustConnect from an allowed and a disallowed peer; the latter must be rejected and audited.
1.6.3Immediately before a write, the actuator shall revalidate request bounds, mode, allowlist, target cgroup, process-instance identity where applicable, and AIOS ownership.MustChange target identity/configuration after policy admission; actuator must reject the stale or mismatched request without writing.
1.6.4For an admitted resource change, the matching adapter shall capture the prior value, apply only the bounded approved value, and read back the effective value. CPU, RAM, and supported I/O use separate capability gates.MustFor allowed and rejected cases, compare prior/requested/read-back values and audit the result.
1.6.5If a write or verification fails, the adapter shall attempt only a guarded restoration of a still-verified AIOS-owned target and shall never invoke an arbitrary shell command.MustInject write/read-back failure and target change; verify guarded restore only for the unchanged owned target, otherwise fail closed.

1.7 Audit and fallback

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.7.1The audit path shall record decisions, denials, authentication/validation failures, action attempts, verification outcomes, and fallback events with correlation context.MustTrace a normal, denied, failed, and fallback scenario from input reference to outcome without asserting physical schema.
1.7.2Audit records shall be appended to a hash-chained log whose verification can detect modification, missing links, or reset history.MustAlter, remove, and reset a test record; verification must flag each case and actuation must remain disabled pending review.
1.7.3A watchdog shall monitor service heartbeat and input freshness independently of the ordinary decision path.MustStop a heartbeat and age input beyond the reviewed test threshold; verify watchdog detects both conditions.
1.7.4On stale evidence, watchdog failure, or unsafe state, AIOS shall block new OS writes, enter fallback, and record a reason.MustInject each condition and verify no new write is admitted and an auditable fallback state is reported.
1.7.5Fallback restoration shall use only the captured prior value for the same resource and target whose cgroup identity and AIOS ownership still match; the restored value shall be read back and verified. A missing or mismatched baseline fails closed.MustTest matching and changed targets; restore and verify only the matching target, otherwise remain fail-closed and report degraded state.

1.8 Read-only dashboard

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.8.1The dashboard shall expose read-only status, recommendations, operating mode, service health, safety state, action outcomes, and audit summaries through projections.MustDemonstrate each view from read-only data and confirm no view requires a control call.
1.8.2The dashboard shall provide no command, approval, policy edit, mode change, or resource-control operation, and shall not provide a path to the actuator socket.MustReview the UI, routes, service identity, and access rights; verify no control affordance or connection exists.
1.8.3The dashboard shall present measured zero separately from unavailable, stale, degraded, warming-up, and denied data.MustUse fixtures for every data-quality state and verify distinct labels/visual states.

1.9 Deployment and optional CPU placement

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
1.9.1systemd shall supervise proposed service lifecycle and expose service health/failure state to the read-only projection.MustStop/restart each proposed service and verify supervision and health reporting without enabling actuation.
1.9.2As an optional host-local profile, selected non-safety AIOS compute services may be restricted to a host-selected set of online logical CPUs; the effective mask shall be checked.CouldCompare configured and effective CPU masks under parent restrictions; report unsupported or empty masks and return to the safe profile.
1.9.3As an optional host-local profile, CPUQuota/cpu.max may cap aggregate CPU time for selected non-safety AIOS compute services; the watchdog, policy, and actuator shall not receive an unvalidated tight quota.CouldInspect the effective quota and measure heartbeat/fallback under the reviewed profile; report quota as a ceiling, not reserved CPU capacity.
1.9.4AIOS shall report Ubuntu, kernel, cgroup-v2, PSI, and optional eBPF prerequisites and shall disable or degrade unsupported features explicitly.MustRun with supported and unsupported prerequisites; verify reported state and safe fallback for each optional feature.

6. Quality requirements

Quality requirements constrain privilege, safe failure, availability, privacy, performance measurement, compatibility, usability, maintainability, and evidence quality. Numeric acceptance limits remain open until target-host measurements are available.

Security and privacy

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
2.1.1Service permissions shall follow least privilege; only the narrow actuator process may receive the approved cgroup write permission.MustInspect process identities, file permissions, and cgroup access; attempt an unauthorized write from other services.
2.1.2Collector, inference, decision/policy, actuator, audit, and dashboard access shall be separated at the process/interface boundary appropriate to the deployed profile.MustReview the deployment and verify each component has only the required read/write interfaces.
2.1.3The system shall make audit-chain breaks, missing history, resets, or unverifiable events visible and disable actuation until review.MustIntroduce each integrity failure; verify visible state and no further action admission.
2.4.1By default, telemetry and dashboard projections shall use an opaque host alias and process identity; command lines, environment variables, usernames, filesystem paths, and payload contents shall be omitted.MustInspect captured records and dashboard output for prohibited fields; verify host alias use.

Safety and availability

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
2.2.1Invalid, stale, unauthenticated, out-of-bounds, wrong-target, or integrity-failed evidence shall produce LEAVE/deny and no OS write.MustRun the negative safety acceptance suite and confirm zero accepted disallowed writes.
2.2.2Failure of AIOS services shall not replace Linux-native scheduling or memory-management behavior; watchdog/control shall remain outside any unvalidated CPU cap.MustStop or constrain each service in a controlled host run; record native behavior, watchdog freshness, and foreground effect.
2.2.3A service restart shall not enable control unless the reviewed host-local configuration and required safety health are valid.MustRestart from missing, invalid, and valid reviewed configurations; verify safe mode is retained in the first two cases.

Performance and measurement

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
2.3.1Evaluation records shall include AIOS CPU use, RSS, storage and write rate, sample freshness, decision latency, and foreground workload impact.MustProduce a benchmark record containing each named measure and the baseline/configuration metadata.
2.3.2Sampling, staleness, latency, storage, and control thresholds shall be approved from target-host measurements before active control is enabled.MustReview recorded baseline, percentile calculations, and owner approval before any control profile is enabled.

Compatibility

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
2.5.1The deployment shall report prerequisite availability by Ubuntu/kernel/cgroup/PSI/eBPF capability and shall not silently assume every optional interface exists.MustInspect compatibility report on target and on a configuration lacking an optional interface.

Usability

2.6.1The read-only view shall visibly distinguish observation, prediction/recommendation, admitted action, denial, and fallback outcome without offering user control.MustTask-based comprehension review with intended viewers; verify each state is correctly identified and no control path is exposed.

Maintainability

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
2.7.1The design shall keep telemetry collection, validation, inference adaptation, decision policy, IPC, actuation, persistence, audit, watchdog, and dashboard query responsibilities separately reviewable.ShouldArchitecture review maps each responsibility to a bounded component and a documented interface; exact class/API signatures remain implementation decisions.

Evidence and verification

IDRequirementPriorityVerification / acceptance
2.8.1Each leaf requirement shall have a planned verification method and a status that separates proposed design, implemented behavior, and collected evidence.MustAudit the requirements register; every row has a verification method and truthful status/evidence reference.

7. External interfaces and logical data

BoundaryRequirement-level behaviorOpen detail
Host observationsRead supported CPU, memory, I/O, PSI, and process context; preserve units, timestamps, scope, and quality.Exact supported field set and kernel-version matrix.
InferenceGeneric observation context enters; generic prediction outputs leave; no model-specific contract is frozen.AI team owns exact contract and timing/label semantics.
Telemetry storageAccepted data is locally stored in SQLite with reviewed retention/storage bounds.Physical tables, indexes, WAL policy values, and retention duration.
Actuator IPCHost-local Unix domain socket; peer identity checked with SO_PEERCRED; actuator repeats validation.Socket path, payload fields, UID/GID rule, and failure response.
OS controlFixed adapters apply only bounded CPU, RAM, or supported I/O controls on approved cgroups, verify read-back, and use resource-specific guarded recovery.Exact bounds, cgroup ownership, account permissions, and target eligibility.
DashboardFastAPI serves read-only projections and never reaches actuator or cgroup writes.Routes, bind address, authentication, and viewer roles.

Logical entities include host/run context, telemetry observations, process-instance identity, generic prediction output, per-process decision, action outcome, and audit event. These are conceptual relationships, not an approved physical schema or API contract.

8. Verification and release gates

GateEvidence required before passing
Requirement reviewTeam confirms scope, priority, candidate stakeholder groups, and unresolved interfaces; all changes are cross-referenced by hierarchical ID.
Observe-only prototypeCollection, quality states, SQLite bounds, generic inference integration, read-only dashboard, and measured AIOS overhead are demonstrated without OS writes.
Security reviewPeer policy, target allowlist, cgroup ownership, privilege boundaries, audit integrity, and dashboard isolation are reviewed.
Failure and recovery reviewStale inputs, PID reuse, malformed request, unauthorized peer, disk pressure, failed write/read-back, and watchdog loss yield specified no-write or guarded recovery outcomes.
Control enablementApproved bounds, target cgroups, resource budget, effective CPU mask/quota if used, rollback ownership, and measured foreground impact are recorded before enabling any profile.
Market validationEthics direction, consent, actual participant responses, contradictory evidence, and a trace from need hypotheses to requirements/features are documented; technical documentation is not substituted for user evidence.

9. Open decisions

DecisionWhy it remains open
Project type and target segmentThe team has not collectively selected research/product framing or validated which candidate operating context matters most.
Inference input/output semanticsModel owner and team must agree timing, labels, quality context, and fields without model internals being imposed here.
Thresholds and resource budgetsSampling, freshness, cooldown, action bounds, storage retention, CPU/RSS, and latency gates require target-host measurements.
Eligible cgroups, peer identity, and service accountsThese choices control privilege and ownership and require host/security review.
CPU placement profileAffinity restricts eligible logical CPUs; CPUQuota is a cap, not a reservation. Topology and safety-path latency must be measured.
Dashboard roles and deployment exposureNo role names, network binding, or authentication model are assumed.
Market and user evidenceLocal interviews/survey have not been collected; need hypotheses remain unvalidated.

Source: 02_Requirements/Requirement_ID_Crosswalk.csv

03 Problem context and alternatives

The market analysis contains candidate operating contexts and need hypotheses. Technical literature establishes available mechanisms; local demand and measured benefit remain separate evidence questions.

Scope of the evidence

Requirements and market traceability

Requirements baseline

The SRS now uses hierarchical leaf identifiers such as 1.1.2. Each leaf expresses one proposed shall requirement and includes a priority, verification method, provisional stakeholder groups, evidence basis, limitation, and status. Requirement_ID_Crosswalk.csv maps the former FR/NFR identifiers to the new baseline so references in earlier artifacts remain traceable. Use the dotted numeric identifiers for new work.

The SRS is a proposed design baseline, not evidence of implementation. Exact API contracts, physical schemas, role names, numeric thresholds, cgroup targets, and model internals remain unapproved or outside this SRS.

Broader market scope

Candidate_Market_Segments.csv describes five candidate operating contexts, not validated customer segments. Market_Need_to_Feature_Traceability.csv contains 18 hypotheses connecting those contexts to technical evidence, alternatives, proposed features, hierarchical requirements, and local validation questions. Market_Alternatives_Traceability.csv compares technical approaches without claiming market share or product superiority.

Evidence classes distinguish official technical documentation, prior systems research, and project hypotheses. PSI/cgroup/systemd/Kubernetes references establish available mechanisms and constraints; they do not demonstrate local demand, adoption, willingness to pay, AIOS accuracy, safety, or performance. No local survey or interview responses are included. There are no TAM/SAM/SOM or market-size estimates.

Validation path

Use the existing anonymous interview template only after supervisor/course ethics direction. Record consent and candidate context without collecting unnecessary identifying data. Update hypothesis status only when actual responses or controlled measurements are available; preserve contradictory and negative results.

Candidate contexts

MS-01
Segment ID
MS-01
Candidate operating context
Interactive Ubuntu/Linux desktops and workstations
Need hypothesis
Candidate context where CPU or memory pressure may affect foreground responsiveness.
Current alternatives / workaround hypothesis
Manual monitoring, desktop/system monitor tools, OS scheduling, and operator action; exact locally used tools are unknown.
Potential AIOS fit
Process-aware pressure view and, only if approved, bounded CPU-weight policy.
Evidence and limitation
Technical fit: PSI/cgroups documentation [S1,S2]. No evidence that this segment wants AIOS.
Local validation plan
Short interviews across experience bands; ask for a recent pressure episode, detection method, impact, and trust boundary.
MS-02
Segment ID
MS-02
Candidate operating context
Shared development, build, test, or research Linux hosts
Need hypothesis
Candidate context where concurrent jobs may compete for CPU and make diagnosis or prioritization difficult.
Current alternatives / workaround hypothesis
Existing cgroup/systemd controls and manual job scheduling; frequency and cost are unmeasured.
Potential AIOS fit
Per-process/group observations, reasoned LEAVE/proposal, audit, and safe CPU-weight profile.
Evidence and limitation
Mechanism evidence: cgroups/systemd [S2,S3]. Prior scheduling research [S7,S8]. Demand remains unvalidated.
Local validation plan
Interview host users/owners; collect anonymized workload type, impact, existing workaround, and acceptable automation.
MS-03
Segment ID
MS-03
Candidate operating context
Constrained or edge Ubuntu/Linux nodes
Need hypothesis
Candidate context where AIOS resource overhead could be material and host configuration may be limited.
Current alternatives / workaround hypothesis
Static systemd/cgroup settings and remote monitoring; local practices are unknown.
Potential AIOS fit
Observe-only baseline, explicit overhead budgets, and optional compute-service CPU cap/placement experiment.
Evidence and limitation
Technical trade-off evidence from CPU control and affinity docs [S3,S6]. No host-specific fit or benefit measured.
Local validation plan
Use resource budget template and compare AIOS overhead against each target workload; do not infer market demand from hardware constraints.
MS-04
Segment ID
MS-04
Candidate operating context
Single-node or containerized Linux services governed by cgroups
Need hypothesis
Candidate context where resource groups are visible but may already be managed by a runtime or orchestrator.
Current alternatives / workaround hypothesis
cgroup-v2/systemd controls; Kubernetes requests/limits when Kubernetes is present [S11].
Potential AIOS fit
Operate only on explicitly approved workload cgroups and avoid competing with a higher-level controller.
Evidence and limitation
Technical evidence: cgroup/systemd/Kubernetes resource behavior [S2,S3,S11]. AIOS orchestration integration is out of scope unless separately agreed.
Local validation plan
Interview operators; identify control ownership and conflicts before selecting any cgroup target.

Segment ID
MS-05

University labs and shared demonstration hosts
Need hypothesis
Candidate context for reproducible demonstrations and resource attribution across controlled workloads.

Manual observation and fixed host configuration; no institutional workflow is assumed.

Read-only status/audit and repeatable test scenarios; no student-facing control panel.
Evidence and limitation
Project/rubric context only; no external evidence of adoption or local need.

Supervisor-approved, consented interviews and controlled workload comparison; responses not yet collected.

04 Architecture and C4 views

The canonical C4 architecture is the original service-oriented design, refreshed without horizontal layer bands. Separate services handle telemetry, inference, policy, safety monitoring, actuation, and read-only presentation; telemetry and audit data have distinct stores. The design follows the full monitor → process → predict → decide → guarded action path.

Level 1 — System Context

AIOS is shown with the Sysadmin/SRE, selected target workloads, and Ubuntu/Linux host. Human access is read-only. The host exposes observation and resource-control interfaces; all control actions remain proposed and independently gated.

Level 2 — Container Architecture

The container view shows runnable services and data stores inside one AIOS system boundary. It does not treat C4 as a layered architecture. The main view emphasizes the primary monitor-to-action path; four focused container views show the remaining dashboard, telemetry, audit, policy, and watchdog connections on diagrams. Persistent stores use database-cylinder shapes; application containers use labeled rounded rectangles.

Level 3 — Components by service

Each component diagram scopes exactly one C4 container. Components use compact paired upper-left UML1 tabs and required/provided ports. Dashed labeled arrows show project dependency direction across the named interfaces. The actuator remains the only proposed host resource writer.

Runtime behavior and deployment

The dynamic view describes one monitor-to-action scenario; the deployment view places proposed service and data containers on a single Ubuntu 24.04 host. These views do not replace the static C4 context, container, or component diagrams.

Linux controls and evidence limits

Observations use procfs and PSI, including /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}. Candidate cgroup v2 controls are cpu.weight, memory.high, and supported io.weight/io.max. The collector is read-only; the actuator checks peer identity, request bounds, target identity, and controller support before writes, then reads back and records outcomes. The design has not yet established target-host safety or performance benefit.

See the C4 architecture index, the notation review, C4 notation, Linux PSI, and Linux cgroup v2.

These views explain workflow, authentication, deployment, trust boundaries, logical storage, operating states, action safeguards, CPU placement, and the object responsibilities behind the architecture.

%% Sequence calls and replies follow control flow; exact messages remain proposed
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant C as Collector
  participant DB as SQLite telemetry + projection store
  participant I as Inference Services
  participant D as Decision Builder
  participant P as Policy Gate
  participant S as Unix Domain Socket
  participant A as Actuator / peer authenticator
  participant OS as Ubuntu OS
  participant L as Audit Log
  participant W as Watchdog
  participant B as Human Browser
  participant F as Read-only Dashboard API
  C->>C: Collect and validate host/process metrics
  C->>DB: Persist accepted samples
  I->>DB: Read telemetry window
  DB-->>I: Return accepted telemetry window
  I->>D: Generic prediction outputs per process
  D->>DB: Persist recommendation projection for read-only view
  D->>P: Propose LEAVE or bounded action per process
  P->>P: Check host-local mode, target, allowlist, bounds and rate limit
  alt OBSERVE_ONLY, LEAVE, or denied proposal
    P->>L: Append recommendation / decision reason
  else reviewed host-local policy permits bounded CPU control
    P->>S: Connect and send bounded request
    S->>A: Deliver local request
    A->>A: Read peer credentials with SO_PEERCRED
    alt peer not permitted or request invalid
      A-->>S: Reject, no OS write
      S-->>P: Return denial
      A->>L: Append security denial
    else peer and request accepted
      A->>A: Recheck process identity, target, allowlist and bounds
      alt action unsafe or target unavailable
        A-->>S: Deny / no-op
        S-->>P: Return denial
        A->>L: Append denial and reason
      else action safe
        A->>OS: Capture prior value, apply bounded cpu.weight
        OS-->>A: Write result / observable effect
        A->>L: Append action, outcome and hash link
      end
    end
  end
  opt heartbeat stale or unsafe condition
    W->>P: Block new AI proposals
    W->>S: Request bounded rollback through the same local socket
    S->>A: Deliver fallback request
    A->>A: Check watchdog peer with SO_PEERCRED and authorize request class
    A->>A: Recheck recorded target ownership and captured baseline
    alt rollback remains safe
      A->>OS: Restore captured cpu.weight baseline
      OS-->>A: Rollback result
      A->>L: Append fallback and rollback outcome
    else target or baseline no longer verifiable
      A->>L: Append fail-closed fallback, no write
    end
  end
  opt human reads status on separate read-only path
    B->>F: Request status / recommendations / audit view
    F->>DB: Read-only query
    DB-->>F: Current telemetry / recommendation projection
    F->>L: Read-only audit query
    L-->>F: Audit projection
    F-->>B: Display only, no control request is accepted
  end

%% Conceptual UML class model; fields, persistence and multiplicities are not approved schema
classDiagram
direction TB

class HostSample {
  sampleKey: conceptual
  capturedAtUtc: timestamp
  hostMetrics: CPU, memory, PSI
}
class ProcessInstance {
  processRef: proposed stable reference
  pid: observed identifier
  startTime: proposed reuse guard
}
class ProcessSample {
  capturedAtUtc: timestamp
  cpuAndMemory: observed metrics
  ioMetrics: optional
  quality: flags and freshness
}
class PredictionOutput {
  capturedAtUtc: timestamp
  processRef: conceptual link
  output: generic prediction
  uncertainty: if provided
}
class Decision {
  outcome: LEAVE or proposal
  reason: explanation
  status: proposed or denied
}
class ActionExecution {
  action: whitelisted type
  target: approved process group
  priorValue: if captured
  result: applied or denied
}
class AuditEvent {
  eventTime: timestamp
  eventType: conceptual category
  previousHash: chain link
  eventHash: integrity value
}

HostSample "1" -- "0..*" ProcessSample : provides context for
ProcessInstance "1" -- "0..*" ProcessSample : has samples
ProcessInstance "1" -- "0..*" PredictionOutput : receives output
ProcessSample "0..*" -- "0..*" PredictionOutput : contributes input
ProcessInstance "1" -- "0..*" Decision : is target of
PredictionOutput "0..*" -- "0..*" Decision : informs
Decision "1" -- "0..*" ActionExecution : may lead to
Decision "0..1" -- "0..*" AuditEvent : may be recorded by
ActionExecution "0..1" -- "0..*" AuditEvent : may be recorded by

note for ProcessInstance "PID plus process start time is a proposed identity guard against PID reuse; exact keys are not approved."
note for PredictionOutput "Generic output only; model type, algorithm and internal schema remain colleague-owned."
note for AuditEvent "Event categories may include decision, denial, action result and fallback; exact taxonomy, retention and storage remain open."
note for Decision "Conceptual logical model only. SQLite is proposed for accepted telemetry and read-only recommendation projection; this diagram does not approve physical tables."

  OBSERVE_ONLY --> WARNING: stale, uncertain, or pressure condition

  WARNING --> OBSERVE_ONLY: freshness and health checks pass

  OBSERVE_ONLY --> CPU_CONTROL: host-local reviewed policy enables approved CPU cgroup

  CPU_CONTROL --> OBSERVE_ONLY: policy disables control or health gate fails

  WARNING --> FALLBACK: watchdog timeout / unsafe condition

  OBSERVE_ONLY --> FALLBACK: unsafe input / watchdog failure

  CPU_CONTROL --> FALLBACK: IPC, actuator, or watchdog fault

  FALLBACK --> RECOVERY_CHECK: services restarted and safe-state check begins

  RECOVERY_CHECK --> OBSERVE_ONLY: checks pass, CPU control stays disabled

  RECOVERY_CHECK --> FALLBACK: any check fails

  note right of CPU_CONTROL

    Only bounded cpu.weight on a preconfigured approved cgroup.

    Memory and I/O stay recommendations in initial scope.

  end note

  note right of FALLBACK

    Block new AI writes. Restore a captured value only for a verified AIOS-owned target.

    If safe rollback fails, stay fail-closed and report degraded mode.

  end note

  note left of OBSERVE_ONLY

    Default mode. Viewers can read status only.

    The dashboard cannot change mode or authorize actions.

  end note

Detailed explanations of the software views

AIOS Process Aware Software Design

AI-Native Adaptive Operating System | AIU Graduation Project 1

This diagram set expresses AIOS as an autonomous, safe process-level control loop: it collects and validates telemetry, consumes generic prediction outputs, builds a per-process recommendation, and applies only a host-local preconfigured action that passes policy, security, and actuator checks. Human access is a read-only dashboard projection for status, recommendations, and audit history. Users cannot submit commands, approve actions, change mode/policy, or address the control path. Model types and internals remain generic. See AIOS_Component_Rationale_and_Diagram_QA.docx for component reasons/trade-offs and the full arrow/notation review.

Recommended design principles

Prediction is advisory. The decision and policy layers select a no-op or a permitted action; model output never directly calls the operating system.

Keep policy and security checks explicit. Check process eligibility, action whitelist, parameter bounds, and rate limits before authenticated local IPC. The actuator repeats critical checks before applying changes.

Make every action traceable. Record the process reference, input/prediction context, decision reason, denial or action, and observed result in an append-only hash-chained audit log.

Fail safe. Invalid input, unavailable services, stale heartbeat, untrusted peer, unsafe parameters, or uncertain target identity results in LEAVE/deny. The watchdog blocks new writes; the proposed recovery path restores a captured AIOS-owned CPU weight only when target identity and ownership remain valid, then verifies and audits the result. If safe rollback cannot be verified, the system remains fail-closed and reports degraded fallback.

Use bounded OS controls only after review. OBSERVE_ONLY is the default. The proposed final product target includes bounded cpu.weight, memory.high, and supported io.weight/io.max controls on approved cgroups, with separate capability and safety gates. Implementation is phased, with CPU first; unsupported controls remain recommendations. There is no memory.max, process termination, arbitrary command, runtime dashboard setting, or user approval path.

Treat core affinity as an optional deployment profile. Pinning AIOS services to selected logical CPUs constrains where they run, but does not reserve a physical core. Keep AIOS services separate from workload cgroups and benchmark the control path before narrowing the mask. Choose online logical CPU IDs and service grouping for the host, account for SMT siblings, and do not hard-code CPU 0 or assume exclusivity.

What is specified and what remains a design choice

Grounded technologies and controls: Ubuntu 24.04, Python collector with psutil, optional eBPF probes, SQLite telemetry, generic inference/decision responsibilities, Unix domain socket with SO_PEERCRED, bounded cgroups v2/priority controls, FastAPI dashboard, systemd supervision, STRIDE mitigations, whitelist, input validation, append-only/hash-chained audit log, and watchdog fallback.

The available technical material does not define exact API contracts, socket message formats, model algorithms, schema, process identity key, per-process eligibility list, numeric resource bounds, rate-limit values, dashboard authentication/network exposure, or fallback timing. These diagrams mark such items as proposed or unspecified rather than inventing project facts. The dashboard is designed query-only and has no actuator socket or cgroup-write permission.

OBSERVE_ONLY is the default, and all resources may produce recommendations. The final product target supports separately gated bounded CPU, RAM, and supported I/O control on approved cgroups. Implementation is phased, with CPU first; RAM and I/O follow controller, host, workload, and recovery review.

UML notation and lecture conventions

In UML class views, plain solid lines are associations with conceptual multiplicities; dashed open-arrow lines are dependencies pointing to the supplier; dashed hollow-triangle lines are interface realizations. Use-case actor associations are unarrowed. These follow standard UML and the supplied lecture notation.

UML use follows OMG UML 2.5.1. PlantUML provides the formal UML component, use-case, activity, and deployment views: dependencies point from client to supplier, actor associations are unarrowed, activity decisions use guarded outgoing flows, and deployment communication paths are unarrowed. Mermaid sequence, class, and state views use UML-style syntax and are not claimed as full OMG UML interchange models; sequence calls are solid and replies dashed. Context, flowchart, DFD-style, and C4 views retain their own notation. Diagram 09 uses labeled solid directed data/control flows. C4 is a separate architecture notation. See AIOS_Diagram_Notation_Audit.md for the view register and official references.

Object-oriented design and SOLID

Single Responsibility is reflected by separate collection, validation, decision, policy, actuation, audit, watchdog, and dashboard-query responsibilities. Open/Closed is supported through reviewed adapters and policy strategies; any new control still requires explicit bounds and security review. Liskov Substitution means each adapter must preserve the port’s safety guarantees, including explicit missing data and rejection of unsafe values.

Interface Segregation separates telemetry writes, inference reads, audit appends, audit queries, and dashboard reads. The FastAPI read-only adapter has no policy, actuator, or operating-system control interface. Dependency Inversion keeps application services dependent on ports rather than psutil, SQLite, Unix sockets, or cgroups v2 details.

Patterns chosen for AIOS

Ports and Adapters (hexagonal architecture) keeps platform integrations at system edges. Adapter and Repository patterns isolate psutil/procfs, optional fixed eBPF, SQLite, Unix-socket IPC, FastAPI, and the fixed cgroups v2 CPU-weight interface. Strategy makes OBSERVE_ONLY the default policy and leaves optional bounded CPU control behind reviewed host-local configuration. Delegation favors small collaborators over inheritance where components use one another rather than form an is-a hierarchy.

The watchdog acts as a safety supervisor: it blocks new writes on stale or unsafe operation and requests rollback only for a still-verified AIOS-owned target. All class and pattern choices are proposed design; exact API contracts, socket messages, SQLite schema, and implementation status are not implied. Component reasons/trade-offs and the 15-diagram notation review are in AIOS_Component_Rationale_and_Diagram_QA.docx; the SOLID mapping is in OOD_SOLID_and_Design_Patterns.md.

Defines separate control and viewing paths. The autonomous AIOS core observes, assesses, and may apply only preconfigured bounded CPU control after policy/security gates. A human viewer receives status through the read-only dashboard projection; there is no user command, approval, policy-edit, or mode-switch path. Exact viewer roles and deployment exposure remain unspecified.

Neither reserves a physical core. Exact service grouping and contracts remain design choices.

Defines a recommendation-first action catalog. OBSERVE_ONLY is default. Unsupported controls remain recommendations. There is no memory.max, process termination, arbitrary command, or dashboard control. Adds core placement as optional host-local deployment configuration. CPUAffinity= or AllowedCPUs= constrains eligible logical CPUs; the effective set depends on parent cgroups and online CPUs. Pinning does not isolate or reserve a physical core. Profile C pairs affinity with a CPUQuota ceiling; it does not reserve a slice. Keep watchdog, policy, and actuator outside an unvalidated tight quota. Evaluate latency, freshness, foreground impact, and heartbeat health before a narrow mask.

06 Component choices and object design

Technology choices are justified in terms of responsibilities, trade-offs, and constraints. Ports and adapters keep Linux and storage details outside core policy logic.

Component rationale and trade-offs

AIOS Component Rationale and Diagram QA

Review date: 14 November 2026 | Status: proposed design, not implementation evidence

This note explains why the proposed components are included, their costs and limits, and the consistency/notation review of all 15 editable diagrams. It does not claim implementation, Ubuntu 24.04 target validation, experimental benefit, or a guaranteed grade.

1. Consistency corrections made

Inference and dashboard arrows now show read requests; SQLite returns telemetry/projection data and does not push it. SQLite is proposed for bounded telemetry plus a read-only recommendation projection; audit is a separate logical store.

Watchdog rollback now uses the same authenticated Unix socket as normal requests. The actuator checks SO_PEERCRED and revalidates the target and saved baseline before a restore.

The Ubuntu deployment view draws systemd within the host and separates affinity from CPUQuota. The optional tight quota applies only to the reviewed compute slice; watchdog, policy, and actuator stay outside it.

The context label now says faults stop further AIOS writes, not ordinary host writes. Use-case actor associations are unarrowed.

The logical model, action branches, and DFD distinguish conceptual schema, data reads/writes, separate CPU/RAM/I/O gates, and bounded cgroup control.

2. Why each component is used

These are proposed choices unless identified as a Linux/platform mechanism. Exact thresholds, identities, schemas, privileges, and interfaces still need team/host review.

ComponentWhy includedTrade-off / boundary / open point
Ubuntu 24.04 + LinuxStated host target; AIOS is a user-space supervisor and lets Linux keep scheduler/resource enforcement.Target behavior is not verified by the included Ubuntu 26.04.1 VM sample. Record target kernel, systemd, topology, and cgroup mode. [R4, R10]
PythonOne proposed runtime for collection and service adapters keeps a first prototype and psutil integration straightforward.This is a fit assumption, not a performance result; measure each service and inference runtime.
psutil collectorPython APIs expose system and process measurements, reducing custom parsing AIOS would otherwise own. [R5]Permissions, disappearing processes, resets, and platform-specific fields remain; represent missingness explicitly.
/proc/pressure (PSI)CPU, memory, and I/O PSI quantify time tasks are stalled under resource pressure, complementing utilization. [R6]PSI is current pressure, not a prediction. Availability and scope depend on the running kernel.
Optional fixed eBPF probesCan add a reviewed kernel event/counter not exposed cleanly by ordinary polling.Privileges, verifier constraints, kernel compatibility, overhead, and maintenance justify disabled-by-default use. [R7]
Input validator + identityFreshness, units, plausibility, source health, and PID plus process start time are checked before inference/action.Exact key, tolerance, and stale thresholds remain open. Unknown or ambiguous identity means LEAVE/deny.
SQLite local repositorySQLite (the name is SQLite, not LiteSQL) is an in-process, serverless, transactional, local-file database. It avoids a separate database server for a single-host prototype and can support bounded telemetry queries and recommendation projections. [R1, R2]Only one write transaction runs at a time; WAL can allow readers alongside a writer. Measure insert/query rates, WAL/checkpoint cost, and storage growth. Reassess if concurrency, scale, or multi-host needs exceed this fit. [R3]
Generic inference servicesDefines a stable model-independent boundary for generic per-process prediction outputs while leaving AI model types, algorithms, and internals to the colleague.Model contract, footprint, accuracy, and benefit are unapproved/unverified. Predictions are advisory and have no OS write capability.
Per-process decision builderCombines generic outputs with current host/process context to produce a reasoned recommendation or LEAVE for each eligible process.Eligibility, reason fields, and uncertainty handling need team agreement; keeping it separate prevents a raw model output from becoming an action.
Policy gateCentral admission point for mode, target, allowlist, freshness, bounds, and cooldown. OBSERVE_ONLY is default; approved host-local config may admit only the bounded CPU action.Policy values and owner are open. A denial must be auditable and produce no partial OS write.
Unix socket + SO_PEERCREDHost-local privileged handoff; Linux returns credentials of the connected peer to the receiver. [R8]Peer identity does not validate payload or target. UID/GID policy and message format are open; actuator repeats request/target checks.
Actuator / resource managerNarrow fixed adapter is the only proposed OS writer; it rechecks identity, ownership, and bounds immediately before an allowed write.No shell or arbitrary path. Service privileges, cgroup allowlist, value range, and rollback ownership require review.
cgroups v2 cpu.weightInitial implementation candidate: bounded cpu.weight on an approved workload cgroup; final product target includes separately gated RAM and supported I/O controls. [R4]Relative share among active siblings under contention—not a CPU-time cap, minimum, or exclusive core. Impact applies to the entire target group.
Separate RAM and I/O capability gatesVisible to decision/dashboard projections. Bounded memory.high and supported I/O controls are part of the final target after their separate host, capability, safety, and recovery gates pass. memory.max and process termination are excluded.These controls can destabilize or starve workloads; active use needs separate policy, privilege, rollback, and workload testing.
Hash-chained audit logRecords decisions, denials, actions, results, verification, and fallback for traceability.A hash chain is not automatically tamper-proof: a local attacker able to rewrite the whole store may rebuild it. Protect ownership/checkpoints and review physical backend, rotation, and retention.
Watchdog / heartbeatDetects stale/unsafe operation, blocks new AIOS proposals, and requests verified rollback through the same authenticated socket.Not the same as systemd and cannot make an unsafe restore safe. If ownership/baseline is uncertain, fail closed and report degraded mode.
systemd supervisionProposed Ubuntu service lifecycle/restart supervision and host-local unit/slice resource settings.Restart is not recovery and must not enable control. Unit names, dependencies, and permissions are not implemented or approved.
FastAPI read-only adapterProposed Python web boundary for presenting status/recommendation/audit projections; official docs describe a Python type-hint-based API framework. [R9]No command, approval, settings, policy, mode, socket, or cgroup-write interface. Routes, auth, bind address, and exposure remain open.
Recommendation projectionA compact read model gives the dashboard persisted recommendations without entering the decision or actuator path.Proposed logical projection only; physical fields, retention, and exact schema remain open.
Human viewer boundaryProvides visibility into status, health, mode, recommendations, and audit while preserving autonomous control.Human is associated only with view use cases; no command or approval path exists. Role names and access policy are TBD.

3. CPU placement: different controls, different guarantees

The “part of a specific core” idea is an optional host-local experiment for selected compute units. No option guarantees an exclusive fraction of a physical core. Keep watchdog, policy, and actuator outside an unvalidated tight quota.

MechanismWhat it doesWhat it does not promise / guard
Affinity / AllowedCPUsRestricts where selected services may run on online logical CPUs.Placement only; parent cgroups may narrow the effective set; other tasks may share the CPU. [R10, R11]
CPUQuota / cpu.maxCaps the configured unit’s CPU time; an illustrative 20% on a single-CPU set is a 0.2 CPU-equivalent ceiling.Ceiling, not a reservation or minimum; can delay work. Exclude the safety path until tested. [R4, R10]
cpu.weightChanges relative CPU-cycle distribution among active sibling cgroups; used for approved workload-group priority.Relative share, not an absolute amount or quota; distinct from CPUQuota. [R4]
Isolated physical corePossible later host-level interference study.Invasive; requires SMT/topology, IRQ, housekeeping, boot/cpuset, operations, and rollback review.

4. Arrow and notation audit: all 15 diagrams

DiagramNotation and arrow review
01 · ContextLabeled host/core/dashboard flows; input and output directions are explicit. Viewer ends at read-only dashboard. Fault means stop AIOS writes, not host writes.
02 · ArchitectureLabeled sample, query/result, decision, IPC, control, audit, and read-only paths. SQLite is passive; watchdog rollback uses the same authenticated IPC.
03 · ComponentsArrows distinguish persistence, repository reads/results, policy admission, IPC, OS write, audit, and dashboard reads. Removed misleading kernel-to-database write; systemd details are in deployment.
04 · Use casesActor-to-use-case associations are plain unarrowed lines. Three view-only cases; no unsupported include/extend or control case.
05 · ActivityAction boxes, decision diamonds, and labeled guards; invalid input, OBSERVE_ONLY, denial, safe CPU action, and rollback have outcomes. Rollback re-enters peer check and actuator validation.
06 · Per-processLEAVE and OBSERVE_ONLY remain distinct from bounded CPU, RAM, and supported I/O control branches. Each resource uses its own capability gate; watchdog recovery is authenticated and rechecks target/baseline.
07 · SequenceSolid calls/messages, dashed replies, alt/opt conditions. Actuator receives SO_PEERCRED; watchdog uses same socket and rechecks target/baseline.
08 · DeploymentUbuntu host/service grouping; systemd is inside host. Affinity and CPUQuota are separate; optional cap excludes watchdog/policy/actuator.
09 · DFD / trustDirectional sample writes, read requests/results, bounded writes, and audit events cross labeled trust boundaries. Dotted links identify safety/read-only paths.
10 · Logical modelClass rectangles, plain associations, conceptual multiplicities, and notes; no navigability arrows or composition diamonds imply an approved physical schema.
11 · Operating statesInitial pseudostate, named modes, and labeled transitions. Recovery returns to OBSERVE_ONLY, never automatic CPU_CONTROL.
12 · Action guardBranches distinguish recommendation, deny, separately gated CPU/RAM/I/O actions, and rollback. Unsupported controls remain recommendations; rollback uses the authenticated socket.
13 · CPU profileProfiles feed the same matched measurement and safety gate. Affinity, CPUQuota, cpu.weight, and isolated-core research are not conflated.
14 · Application class modelDashed open-arrow dependencies point to required ports; hollow-triangle dashed arrows show interface realization. No false inheritance/composition.
15 · Dashboard class modelViewer association is unarrowed; dashed dependencies and hollow-triangle realizations are consistent UML. Only query ports are exposed.

5. Open decisions and evidence limits

Team/host/security agreement is still needed for the Ubuntu 24.04 target host; model interface; service identities and UID/GID allowlist; socket payload; physical SQLite schema; audit backend/checkpoint/retention; cadence and bounds; approved process-to-cgroup mapping; CPU IDs and quota grouping; eBPF privileges; and dashboard routes, authentication, and network binding.

The included Linux capture is a passive Ubuntu 26.04.1 VM sample, not Ubuntu 24.04 compatibility evidence, an AIOS trace, a controlled benchmark, or a safety result. Budgets and thresholds remain proposals until measured and reviewed.

[R11] systemd.exec — https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/latest/systemd.exec.html

Official documentation accessed 14 November 2026. These sources establish platform/library behavior, not AIOS implementation, host fit, safety, or performance.

Object design SOLID and design patterns

AIOS Object Design and Software Principles

Purpose and status

This note explains the proposed object design behind Diagrams 10, 14, and 15. The diagrams use standard notation for their purpose: UML classes for static structure, UML use cases for the human boundary, and the existing activity, sequence, deployment, data-flow, and state notations for runtime behavior. These are design proposals, not claims that the classes or interfaces have already been implemented.

AIOS remains autonomous. A human can only read status, recommendations, operating mode, safety health, and audit projections through the dashboard. There is no user command, action approval, policy edit, or mode-change path to the control plane.

UML conventions

The class views follow the CSE454 UML lecture conventions: class rectangles with names and only the conceptual attributes needed to explain the model; solid, labeled associations with multiplicities at both ends; and no navigation arrow unless one-way access is an intentional part of the design. Diagram 10 therefore uses plain associations. Diagrams 14 and 15 use dashed dependency arrows for “uses” relationships and hollow-triangle realization arrows where an adapter or service fulfills an interface.

Generalization is reserved for a genuine “is-a” relationship. Aggregation and composition diamonds are omitted because the current design does not specify whole-part lifecycle ownership. Method signatures, API routes, socket message formats, exact SQLite tables, and model-specific fields are omitted because the source material does not define them.

SOLID and object-oriented design

PrincipleProposed application in AIOS
Single ResponsibilityCollection, validation, decision building, policy admission, OS control, audit writing, watchdog supervision, and dashboard projection have separate responsibilities.
Open/ClosedNew telemetry sources and reviewed resource adapters can be added behind ports. A new control still requires an explicit policy, security review, bounds, and target checks.
Liskov SubstitutionEvery implementation of a port must preserve its safety meaning. Missing or unsupported telemetry stays explicit; an adapter must not turn it into a successful value or bypass bounds.
Interface SegregationCollection writes, inference reads, dashboard reads, audit appends, and audit queries use separate interfaces. The FastAPI viewer has no command or actuator interface.
Dependency InversionApplication services depend on ports. psutil/procfs, optional fixed eBPF probes, SQLite, Unix sockets, FastAPI, and cgroups v2 sit at the edges as adapters.

Composition and delegation are preferred over inheritance. The design does not force Singleton, inheritance hierarchies, or ownership diamonds where they add no value.

Patterns selected for this system

Pattern or approachAIOS useWhy it fits
Hexagonal architecture (Ports and Adapters)Core services depend on telemetry, inference, policy, audit, and actuation ports; platform integrations stay at the boundary.Keeps Linux and storage details out of decision rules and makes privilege boundaries visible.
Adapterpsutil/procfs and optional fixed eBPF inputs; SQLite readers/writers; the Unix-socket client/server; the fixed cgroups v2 resource adapter; and the FastAPI read-only adapter.Translates external mechanisms to narrow application interfaces without giving each component broad OS access.
Repository and read projectionSQLite telemetry and recommendation-projection access are isolated behind repository/read-projection interfaces; audit is separate logical storage.Separates storage details from business decisions and keeps the viewer query-only.
StrategyOBSERVE_ONLY is the default policy strategy; a reviewed host-local strategy may admit bounded CPU-weight control for an approved cgroup.Makes policy variants explicit while preventing the model output or dashboard from choosing privileged controls.
DelegationThe collector delegates validation, the policy gate delegates policy choice, and the actuator delegates OS changes to a fixed resource adapter.Keeps each object small and replaces subclassing where the relationship is “uses,” not “is-a.”
Safety supervisor / watchdogA stale heartbeat or unsafe condition blocks new writes and requests a verified safe fallback through the same guarded local path.Keeps failure handling explicit and fail-closed; it does not create a dashboard bypass or arbitrary rollback.

Diagram assumptions and constraints

Diagram 10 is a conceptual logical model, not an approved database schema. Its multiplicities are proposed to make the expected relationships reviewable. ProcessInstance and the proposed PID-plus-start-time identity guard address PID reuse; the exact key, fields, cardinalities, retention, and normalization remain team decisions. Prediction outputs stay generic, with no model type or algorithm internals.

Diagram 14 shows responsibilities and outbound ports for the autonomous control path. Diagram 15 shows the dashboard query boundary and read-only projections. The class diagrams intentionally omit exact method signatures so they cannot be mistaken for approved API contracts. The final product target includes independently gated bounded CPU, RAM, and supported I/O controls on approved cgroups; implementation is phased, with CPU first. Each request requires policy admission, Unix-domain-socket peer authentication with SO_PEERCRED, and actuator-side revalidation.

Optional placement applies to selected non-safety compute services: affinity restricts eligible logical CPUs; CPUQuota is a separate CPU-time ceiling. Neither reserves a physical core. Watchdog, policy, and actuator stay outside an unvalidated tight quota. See AIOS_Component_Rationale_and_Diagram_QA.docx for full trade-offs and diagram audit.

Source: 01_Diagrams/OOD_SOLID_and_Design_Patterns.md

07 Telemetry interfaces and storage

The interface design preserves timestamps, units, process identity, freshness, and missing-data reasons. Model output and actuator requests cross validation boundaries.

Shared telemetry and prediction interface

AIOS telemetry and shared prediction interface

Proposed draft for team agreement. Model internals and exact API contracts remain with the team.

Target and collection

Target Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, as stated in the technical deep dive.

Python/psutil and read-only procfs PSI; optional fixed eBPF only after security review.

Candidate cadence 1 second, following the technical example; measure overhead and confirm with AI owners.

Include RFC 3339 UTC and monotonic nanoseconds, run ID, opaque host alias and boot ID.

Process reference uses PID plus start time. Omit process name, command line, environment, open files and username by default unless a privacy-reviewed display need is agreed.

Candidate signal groups

AreaInputsHandling
CPUHost/per-core utilization, runnable count, CPU PSI some/full avg10/60/300/totalPreserve units/window; flag unsupported PSI
MemoryMemTotal, MemAvailable, swap, memory PSI, readable fault/reclaim countersBytes/counts; reset-aware deltas
I/ODisk counters, I/O PSI, blocked tasks if availableRaw counters and interval deltas; record device scope
ProcessPID + start time, status, CPU %, RSS, optional I/ONullable; partial visibility is explicit
QualityFreshness, warm-up, unsupported, denied, parse error, resetNull + reason; no zero-fill

JSON Lines is proposed for portable recordings; SQLite is proposed for accepted telemetry and a bounded read-only recommendation projection; the append-only hash-chain audit is a separate logical store. Candidate relational schemas and EERDs are documented in the proposed data-model package; exact fields, JSON envelopes, retention, prediction contract, REST paths and socket messages remain unapproved and require team agreement.

User-facing boundary

Human access is through a read-only dashboard projection for status, recommendations, safety health and audit history.

The dashboard/API has no command, action-submit, action-approval, mode-change, or policy-edit path. It cannot access the actuator socket or write cgroup controls.

Decisions and any permitted bounded control are autonomous and follow host-local reviewed deployment policy. No user approval is requested at runtime.

Authentication, network binding/exposure, exact API routes and viewer role names are not specified; review them before deployment without weakening the query-only boundary.

Proposed safe fallback for bounded control

Before any approved CPU-weight change, capture the current value and target identity in the action/audit record.

On watchdog or unsafe-state entry, block new AI writes. Restore the captured value only if the same target is still valid and remains under AIOS control; verify and audit the result.

If rollback cannot be safely verified, remain fail-closed, report degraded fallback, and require host-side recovery. Never issue a generic shell command or guess a target.

These are proposed design safeguards, not implementation evidence. Numeric bounds, ownership rules and timeout values need security review.

Missing and invalid data

Preserve partial records; unsupported and permission-limited values are null with reason.

Reject malformed/out-of-range values and record quality events.

Detect counter reset and process identity change; do not compute a negative rate across a reset.

Mark first rate sample as warm-up. Never silently forward-fill/interpolate.

Stale required input cannot authorize an action; OBSERVE_ONLY remains available.

Collection is read-only: no process movement, cgroup writes, priority changes, signals or service changes.
